script.base: No spread or total is saved, so this is a form script, not a market script. Indianapolis has lived on Jonathan Taylor (43 carries, 190 yards, 4.42 YPC, 43 of 51 listed rushes) while its dropback EPA is negative (-0.22 unblitzed, -0.02 vs blitz) and Houston blitzes only 18%, so the base case is a competitive game in which IND keeps handing Taylor the ball and the pass game stays short: Tyler Warren has 12 targets but only 10 air yards (13 and 21 receiving yards). Houston, with Nico Collins out plus Ed Ingram out and Trent Brown questionable, is a Dalton Schultz quick game (EPA/db +0.39 vs blitz; IND blitzes 25%) rather than a shootout.
script.flip1: IND leads early behind Taylor and Houston's injured line cannot stay on schedule. Taylor's carries hold or rise to kill clock, so the rush over survives and is helped. Warren's behind-the-line role has even less reason to produce yards, so the under survives. This is the run-clock path even without a saved spread.
script.flip2: Houston's blitz-beater quick game (Schultz, Noel, Hutchinson) jumps ahead and IND is down multiple scores. Taylor's carries collapse: that is the kill for the rush over, so the leg is script-dependent on this flip. Jones throws more; Pierce's vacated 113 air yards fit Downs, Allen and Treadwell, not Warren (0.83 air yards per target). Warren under is hurt only by a chunk YAC play, not by ordinary extra targets.

injury_fallout: HOU OUT WR Nico Collins (hamstring): 10 targets, 75 yards, 120 air yards over weeks 1-2 come off the board. Next men from the target table are Dalton Schultz (already 22/175/130, team leader), Xavier Hutchinson (15/69/169, not converting), Jaylin Noel (7 targets, 84 yards), Jared Wayne (8/45/116) and Kayshon Boutte (7/58/98). HOU OL: G Ed Ingram Out (groin), T Trent Brown Questionable (knee) — pressure up, HOU rush efficiency down (Montgomery 70 yards on 26 carries, 2.69 YPC; Marks 50 on 17, 2.94), more quick throws, deep yards at risk, Stroud scrambles more likely. HOU defense OUT: DE Jadeveon Clowney (knee) weakens the edge vs Taylor; S M.J. Stewart (knee) and LB Jacob Hummel (groin) are the coverage losses that help IND TEs, RBs and the slot — the explicit counter to a Warren under. IND OUT WR Alec Pierce (heel) vacates 7 targets, 72 yards, 113 air yards; same-position absorbers are Josh Downs (13/109/109), Keenan Allen (11/37/53) and Laquon Treadwell (4/61/58; game log 0 and 61). WR Ashton Dulin Out (ankle) is depth. CB Charvarius Ward Questionable (groin) is not ruled out, so no confirmed backup-corner edge. Inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff are not in the pack. Sources: pack nflverse injury report and week 1-2 target/rush tables only.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost. Taylor: Houston, even without Clowney, sells out to the run after back-to-back 90-yard games, holds him near 3.7 YPC, and the flip hits — Stroud and Schultz punish IND's 25% blitz for an early lead, IND is throwing by the second quarter, and Taylor ends at 14-16 carries in the mid-60s. The 81.5 was a two-game heater, and 4.12 YPC allowed says this front was never a giveaway. Warren: the market's 46.5 was the tell, not a stale number. Hummel and Stewart out turn dump-offs into YAC, he adds one 20-plus catch-and-run to a 25-yard floor, and the over cashes. Or IND trails and schemed touches replace the 10-air-yard role the two-game log shows. Ward and Brown are still questionable, inactives are not out, and a morning Out tag is not a lock. If that Warren counter is the one that bothers you, cut only Warren; the Taylor read does not depend on it.
slip_story: One script only: Indianapolis plays its identity, Taylor carries, and the pass game stays supplementary and behind the line, so Warren's 10 air yards stay under 46.5. Run-clock / low-TE-yardage stack, not a shootout. Both legs live in the base and in flip 1 (IND ahead). Flip 2 (HOU ahead big) is the shared stress, worse for Taylor than for Warren. Do not add Schultz, Downs, Hutchinson or Noel overs, a HOU team-total over, or Stroud rush overs — those need Houston to throw and are the other slip. No TD legs. One market per player. Two legs, inside the 3-4 cap. Depth receivers not used.
